scope: SUTRA browser/runtime, evidence pipeline, synthetic action authority/witness laboratory, inference boundary, and planned multi-provider BYOK workspace. This is an executable engineering register, not a security certification.
nonClaims: A model, peer, signature, hash, receipt, witness, or provenance record does not establish factual truth.
The current authority/witness laboratory is not distributed consensus, a public transparency log, trusted time, or a production arbitrary-effect transaction.
Current checked-in inference is disabled by default and BYOK remains disabled; no live provider credential is authorized by this model.
Browser-origin checks are not authentication against non-browser callers.
A privileged attacker able to roll back both authority and witness trust domains can recreate an older mutually consistent state.
Exact credential canary scans detect direct secret echo only; they do not prove resistance to encoded, hashed, fragmented or transformed exfiltration by a compromised trusted adapter.
Fail-closed orphaned admission preserves modeled safety at the cost of availability; clearing or leasing an orphan without proof of non-dispatch can permit duplicate delayed external effects.

Lower raw authority, post-effect witness and legacy grant layers remain laboratory APIs, but they no longer implement http.Handler directly; deliberate custom wrappers or source modification can still bypass the approved composite and remain outside the guarantee.
No real provider or external service is verified to issue or honor SUTRA's permanent non-application closure proof; the current signer is a synthetic separately keyed laboratory authority.

principals.authority: Chooses investigations, explicit consent, provider/model profile and local UI actions. Does not sign machine authority implicitly.
Trusted UI/runtime policy boundary; compiles closed data, injects fixed adapters, and presents consent. Must not delegate authority to model or peer text.
Proposal generation only. No permission to select credentials, destinations, budgets, verification status, action keys or consent.
Publishes bounded public data/graphs. No authority over caller private context, model credential, remote write, or caller consent.
Signs or approves one exact scoped operation. Approval must bind operation, destination, lifetime and authority.
Authenticates callers, owns synthetic action/receipt/contact state and exact expected-head CAS. Single authority, not consensus.
Maintains separately keyed monotonic head and signs challenge-bound attestations. Does not authorize the underlying action.
Fixed same-origin service that validates model requests, reserves bounded resources, and contacts only a configured upstream.
Executes model inference under provider semantics. Provider output and usage reports are untrusted observations until checked.
Future host-owned secret boundary. Exposes opaque handles only; secret values must never become graph/model/peer/trace data.
Read-only bounded synthetic/source capability selected by trusted host policy; cannot widen itself.
Controls deployment/configuration and may provision keys. Operator compromise is outside guarantees that depend on independent operation.
None. May drop, delay, replay, redirect, reorder or tamper with transport bytes.
May replace/corrupt one local store in modeled rollback tests. Coordinated privileged rollback of all trust domains remains open.

boundaries.forbidden: credentials, authority keys, implicit consent, verification authority
provider credentials, private context without exact grant, caller prompt forwarding, remote execution

boundaries.allowed: same-origin bounded model request under fixed contract
boundaries.forbidden: visitor Authorization, arbitrary upstream URL, provider secret, widened token/resource limits

boundaries.allowed: validated bounded request plus server-owned credential
exact host-approved signed request with authenticated caller and expected head
boundaries.forbidden: model-selected action, new-key retry without approval, unsigned mutation
stale parent, previously seen head, unsigned transition

boundaries.allowed: fresh challenge-bound signed witness attestation paired with exact authority response
explicit user setup/remove and opaque handle use
boundaries.forbidden: secret value in DOM logs, graph, prompt, peer payload, trace, URL or telemetry

boundaries.allowed: private local durable store under documented assumptions
boundaries.forbidden: claim that signatures alone prevent privileged coordinated rollback

threats.mechanism: Hostile model/peer text attempts to choose a privileged tool, model, destination, credential or private context field.
threats.invariant: Untrusted text is data; runtime authority comes only from host policy and exact grants.

evidence.test: host model policy overrides hostile peer and caller model hints without credential transfer
runtime gives only explicitly approved field to exact peer model prompts

threats.mechanism: Provider/BYOK secret leaks through model arguments, peer fetch headers, traces, exports, logs, URLs or browser storage.
threats.invariant: Secret values remain in a host-owned credential boundary; downstream receives opaque capability only.

evidence.test: host model policy overrides hostile peer and caller model hints without credential transfer
external MCP host cannot import a provider credential into its transport configuration
fixed upstream, server key and imposed cap; sanitized streaming works end to end

threats.mechanism: Caller or model injects an upstream URL, redirect, credential-bearing URL or nested capability.
threats.invariant: Provider/MCP/action transports pin exact hosts/paths and refuse redirects or arbitrary URLs.

evidence.test: Worker uses Workerd-compatible non-following redirect mode; all redirects are refused before a second contact
untrusted peer graph cannot activate nested remote, MCP, executable, REST or private forwarding

threats.mechanism: Lost response causes blind replay with a fresh key or repeats a previously committed synthetic effect.
threats.invariant: Unknown remains nonterminal; retry uses the same approved logical action; signed receipt/status reconcile before new authority.

threats.mechanism: A valid older signed authority snapshot resets history/contact accounting.
threats.invariant: An independently pinned witness head rejects authority-only rollback.

threats.mechanism: Privileged attacker restores both older valid authority and witness stores, recreating a mutually consistent old pair.
threats.invariant: No current invariant prevents this; guarantee requires independently operated transparency/quorum/freshness beyond both local stores.

threats.mechanism: Captured valid authority response plus signed witness view is replayed to a rolled-back client as if fresh.
threats.invariant: External success requires a client-generated fresh challenge bound into a witness attestation and exact authority response.

threats.mechanism: Process dies after durable intent, authority persistence or witness advancement, leaving two trust domains at different stages.
threats.invariant: Signed durable intent makes every one-step gap classifiable and recoverable; no next acknowledged mutation begins before settlement.

threats.mechanism: Caller receives success after authority mutation but before independent witness convergence.
threats.invariant: Externally accepted acknowledgement is composite and witness-confirmed; formal ack never leads witness.

threats.mechanism: Concurrent callers or restarted clients exceed contact/inference resource ceilings, or ambiguous requests are refunded and replayed.
threats.invariant: Shared authoritative reservation precedes contact; ambiguous admitted work is not refunded automatically.

evidence.test: repeated ambiguous admissions consume bounded daily allowance without any refund or replay
transactional quota caps active concurrency, daily clients and resets on a new UTC day

threats.mechanism: Discovery approval is reused for execution, inputs/destination change after approval, revoked/expired approval dispatches, or fresh key is minted as retry.
threats.invariant: Execution consent must bind exact operation/destination/lifetime/key and be checked immediately before contact.

evidence.test: peer consent denial stops before contact with explicit failure and no fabricated completion

threats.mechanism: Peer URL/name substitution, metadata or return values widen private context grant.
threats.invariant: Private grants bind exact peer URL+network and independent directions with closed field allowlists.

evidence.test: same network name on a different origin does not inherit another peer grant
peer protocol metadata cannot bypass the independent structured return allowlist

threats.mechanism: Rotating client identity evades per-client limits or spoofed Origin consumes public global budget.
threats.invariant: Global ceiling remains authoritative even where client identity is weak; public paid API is not claimed.

evidence.test: direct nonbrowser caller that spoofs allowed Origin still hits client quota before second provider call

threats.mechanism: Duplicate/escaped JSON keys, malformed Unicode, hidden metadata or accessors create different interpretations across layers.
threats.invariant: Closed bounded parser/schema rejects ambiguity before capability or provider contact.

evidence.test: ambiguous request JSON and historical tool arguments fail before quota or upstream
peer runtime option accessors and hidden metadata are refused before model or contact

threats.mechanism: Truncated, redirected, malformed or late provider streams are represented as complete model output.
threats.invariant: Only exact complete bounded SSE with supported terminal reason and DONE can certify completion.

evidence.test: upstream must return a complete exact SSE 200 before streaming or emitting DONE
late upstream response body is disposed and quota lease released once after aborted request

threats.mechanism: Vendored runtime/WASM/toolchain or release artifact differs from reviewed source.
threats.invariant: Pinned vendor inventory, build identities and independent replay gates detect reviewed-artifact drift.

evidence.test: Build isolated Rust WebAssembly support engine

threats.mechanism: Future browser-resident credential is read by XSS, compromised dependency, extension or DOM instrumentation.
threats.invariant: No browser credential storage design is approved yet; BYOK remains disabled until a reviewed host-owned secret boundary is selected.

threats.mechanism: Provider tokenization, failed-call billing or delayed usage differs from SUTRA estimates, converting a request cap into false dollar-budget assurance.
threats.invariant: SUTRA resource reservations are not represented as dollar spend; provider-side controls and observed usage are separate required evidence.

evidence.test: resource ceilings charge admitted work without refund, reject before provider, and preserve other counters

threats.mechanism: An attacker obtains the action-authority signing key or independent-witness signing key and can forge otherwise valid responses, transitions or challenge attestations inside that key's trust domain.
threats.invariant: Distinct authority and witness keys prevent one-key compromise from automatically impersonating both domains, but no current invariant survives compromise of the relevant signing key itself.

evidence.test: Reusing the same witness key with a different genesis is a distinct trust

threats.mechanism: A compromised host-approved provider transport receives the real credential at the secret-release boundary and can exfiltrate, transform or misuse it outside SUTRA's returned-result canary checks.
threats.invariant: Only explicitly host-pinned provider transports may receive a credential; exact-secret canary scans reduce accidental echo but are not data-loss prevention against an already trusted malicious adapter.

evidence.test: caller cannot supply provider endpoint, transport, credential field or unapproved model
provider credential echo is refused and its already-admitted reservation becomes unknown

threats.mechanism: A stale, cloned or cross-provider credential handle is used with another provider/model or a disabled profile, causing the wrong secret or budget identity to be dispatched.
threats.invariant: Opaque handle identity, fixed provider catalog, host-pinned transport, model allowlist and per-profile budget row must agree before secret release.

evidence.test: forged, cloned, stale and cross-provider handles cannot resolve a credential
removing a profile invalidates the credential handle but retains budget audit history
profiles can be registered and disabled dynamically without erasing prior reservations

threats.mechanism: A credential is encoded, hashed, fragmented or otherwise transformed before appearing in model input or provider output, bypassing an exact-string canary check.
threats.invariant: Current exact canary detection is only a regression guard for accidental direct disclosure and must not be represented as general secret DLP.

evidence.test: credential accidentally placed in operation is blocked before budget reservation or transport

threats.mechanism: A pre-effect fence reservation can outlive the coordinator evidence that owned it. Blindly clearing the orphan restores availability but can admit a second writer while a delayed first external effect remains possible; retaining it can deny future admission indefinitely.
threats.invariant: An orphaned reservation must remain fail-closed unless independently verifiable evidence proves the prior effect cannot occur; bounded exhaustion must refuse new reservations without mutating the fence or synthetic effect ledger.

threats.mechanism: A deployment or integration exposes a lower raw authority, post-effect witness, legacy grant layer, or unpinned composite operation as a network write surface, bypassing the returning-client policy pin and strongest pre-effect fenced-grant composition.
threats.invariant: Lower effect-capable layers must not implement http.Handler directly; the anchored fenced-grant composite must not export its unpinned Commit, Status or ProcessAttested methods; legacy write routes on the surviving composite must reject without changing authority, fence or policy state.

threats.mechanism: A compromised, stale or semantically weak closure authority signs 'not applied' for an exact reservation that was already dispatched or can still execute. Clearing that orphan admits another writer while the delayed prior effect remains possible.
threats.invariant: Closure authority key must be distinct from the action-authority and fence keys; proof must bind exact reservation hash, request hash, before/after heads and random token; the contract must mean permanent non-application, not point-in-time absence. If that promise is false, the system must not claim at-most-once safety.

threats.mechanism: A cloned upstream signer plus valid signed snapshot, or restoration of an older valid signed upstream snapshot, can recreate unused local terminal state while a prior physical effect already exists. Each local authority can therefore produce internally valid APPLIED state and receipts for the same identity without global effect uniqueness.
threats.invariant: APPLIED/CLOSED exclusivity and the durable effect budget are scoped to one current non-rolled-back upstream authority history. Signatures alone must never be treated as global freshness, consensus or arbitrary-provider exactly-once evidence.
